subject: psychiatry
title: Performance Anxiety and Behavioral Exposure Therapies

steps.tx: **Performance anxiety**, a discrete circumscribed subtype of social anxiety disorder, manifests exclusively when an individual must perform, speak, or play music before an audience. Somatic distress is driven by an acute sympathetic surge, provoking visible hand tremors, voice quivering, palpitations, dry mouth, and cognitive freezing.
steps.say: Performance anxiety occurs during public speaking or recitals, triggering acute sympathetic tremors, voice shaking, and palpitations.

left.title: Performance Anxiety
points: Normal social functioning in informal settings

right.title: Generalized Social Anxiety
points: Pervasive fear across all social interactions
Avoidance of dining, writing, and meeting people

steps.tx: Propranolol cannot calm racing thoughts, yet it quiets the body that betrays them. By blocking peripheral beta receptors in heart and skeletal muscle, it slows the pulse and damps the fine tremor running through the hands. Performers take it before an audition so shaking fingers and a pounding chest stop feeding the fear. This targeted action is **peripheral beta blockade**, useful only where bodily symptoms dominate the complaint.
steps.say: Propranolol blocks beta receptors in heart and muscle, easing tremor and palpitations during performance.

vis.alt: Diagram of propranolol blocking peripheral beta receptors at the heart and skeletal muscle, reducing tremor and fast heartbeat
vis.caption: Propranolol acting at peripheral beta receptors in the heart and skeletal muscle, slowing the pulse and steadying tremulous hands. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Propranolol in performance anxiety** provides targeted symptomatic relief when administered 30 to 60 minutes before a performance at doses of 10 to 40 milligrams. As a non-selective beta-adrenergic antagonist, propranolol blocks peripheral beta-1 and beta-2 receptors, effectively suppressing somatic tremors, palpitations, and vocal shakiness without impairing cognitive alertness.
steps.say: Propranolol taken one hour before a performance blocks beta receptors, extinguishing tremors and palpitations without causing cognitive sedation.

vis.title: Propranolol Pharmacology Profile
rows: Matches peak plasma concentration to performance onset
Suppresses tremor without causing orthostatic hypotension
Halts tachycardia and peripheral hand tremor
Risk of fatal bronchospasm via beta-2 antagonism

steps.tx: Fears are unlearned in an order the patient helps to build. A **stepwise anxiety hierarchy** lists situations from mildly uncomfortable to terrifying, and systematic desensitisation climbs it one mastered rung at a time paired with relaxation. Skipping to the top rung floods rather than treats and usually ends engagement. The ladder drawn together in session becomes the homework map for weeks of exposure practice between appointments.
steps.say: A hierarchy ladder ranks feared situations from mild to severe for graded exposure. Climbing it rung by rung desensitises without flooding.

vis.alt: Stepwise anxiety hierarchy ladder used in systematic desensitisation and exposure therapy.
vis.caption: A ladder of feared situations rises from mild discomfort to the most feared scene. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Systematic desensitisation** is a classical conditioning behavioral therapy developed by Joseph Wolpe based on the principle of reciprocal inhibition. The core physiological premise asserts that an individual cannot concurrently experience relaxation and anxiety; hence, establishing deep muscular relaxation systematically inhibits conditioned phobic anxiety responses.
steps.say: Systematic desensitisation pairs deep relaxation with a fear hierarchy to extinguish phobias through the mechanism of reciprocal inhibition.

nodes.label: Train patient in Jacobson progressive muscle relaxation
Construct detailed 10 to 15 step graded anxiety hierarchy
Pair relaxation with imaginal exposure to lowest hierarchy item
Ascend hierarchy sequentially once each step elicits zero distress

steps.tx: **Subjective Units of Distress Scale**, abbreviated SUDS, quantifies a patient's perceived anxiety level on a numerical rating scale from zero (complete tranquility) to 100 (catastrophic terror). SUDS ratings guide clinicians through the anxiety hierarchy, advancing to subsequent challenges only when distress drops below 20.
steps.say: The SUDS scale measures anxiety from zero to one hundred. Patients master each hierarchy tier until distress scores consistently drop below twenty.

vis.title: SUDS Rating Framework
rows: Target zone for successful exposure mastery
Hold exposure steady; do not retreat or escape
Never terminate prematurely; allow habituation curve

steps.tx: **Flooding** is an intensive behavioral therapy technique wherein the patient is exposed directly and continuously to the highest-intensity phobic stimulus in vivo or through prolonged imagination without any relaxation pairing. Because physiological panic cannot be maintained indefinitely, autonomic exhaustion and cognitive habituation rapidly extinguish the phobic response.
steps.say: Flooding exposes the patient directly to the most feared stimulus until autonomic exhaustion and habituation naturally dissolve the phobia.

left.title: Flooding Technique
points: Direct presentation of maximal fear stimulus
Patient prevented from escaping the situation

right.title: Systematic Desensitisation
points: High patient comfort and low drop-out rate

steps.tx: **Implosion therapy** is a variant of flooding conducted entirely in imagination, where the therapist presents exaggerated, psychodynamically charged catastrophic scenarios involving the feared object. Exposure continues uninterrupted for up to two hours until the patient's conditioned emotional responsiveness undergoes complete extinction.
steps.say: Implosion therapy presents exaggerated imaginal catastrophic scenarios for prolonged durations until internal conditioned emotional reactions extinguish.

right.title: In Vivo Flooding
points: Actual physical contact with feared object

steps.tx: **In vivo exposure therapy** involves real-world confrontation with feared objects or environments, standing as the undisputed empirical gold standard treatment for agoraphobia and specific phobias. Graded real-world immersion allows corrective reality testing, dismantling superstitious avoidance rituals and rebuilding personal self-efficacy.
steps.say: In vivo exposure therapy requires real-world contact with feared environments, providing the most robust empirical treatment for phobias and agoraphobia.

nodes.label: Establish real-world behavioral target (riding an elevator)
Enter situation and record initial peak SUDS score
Remain in situation until SUDS drops by fifty percent
Consolidate cognitive habituation through daily homework

steps.tx: **Virtual reality exposure therapy** utilizes interactive computer-generated environments to simulate phobic scenarios, such as commercial flight, high bridges, or public auditoriums, with complete therapist control over stimulus parameters. This modality achieves therapeutic outcomes comparable to in vivo exposure while ensuring privacy, safety, and repeatable pacing.
steps.say: Virtual reality exposure provides controlled simulations of flights, heights, and auditoriums, matching in vivo therapy while offering controlled safety.

left.title: Virtual Reality Strengths
points: Complete therapist control of stimulus intensity
Preferred by patients fearful of in vivo exposure
